\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بس} (bas)}{بس (bas)}]{\ur{بس} (bas) — a bus; enough}

\label{lesson:UR-C80-bas}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a station, then the Urdu for a car; a train.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بس}}
\textbf{\ur{بس}} — \emph{bas} — \textquotedblleft{}a bus; enough\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بس}} (\emph{bas}) is two words spelled alike. \emph{bas}, \textquotedblleft{}a bus\textquotedblright{}, is a loan from English \emph{bus}, short for \emph{omnibus}; \emph{bas}, \textquotedblleft{}enough\textquotedblright{}, is usually traced to Persian \emph{bas}, \textquotedblleft{}enough\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مسجد} (masjid)}{مسجد (masjid)}]{\ur{مسجد} (masjid) — a mosque}

\label{lesson:UR-C80-masjid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a bus; enough, then the Urdu for a bridge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مسجد}}
\textbf{\ur{مسجد}} — \emph{masjid} — \textquotedblleft{}a mosque\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مسجد}} (\emph{masjid}) is a loan from Arabic \emph{masjid}, \textquotedblleft{}place of prostration, mosque\textquotedblright{}, which reached Urdu through Persian. Its Arabic root is \emph{s-j-d} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}
